rules: Mountain and elevation patterns constrain rivers and transport.
Climate and water constrain agriculture and settlement density.
Resource extraction requires transport, labor, power and water paths.
Large populations require multiple settlements and service networks, not a single city.
Rural populations consume goods and generate freight even when no individual village is named.
Intercity corridors should follow geography and economic demand rather than connect every node directly.
Every region must connect to planetary aggregates so named geography does not erase unnamed population.
